metric: 01 section 6 M4 -- move precision on the labeled rename corpus, >= 0.95, ambiguous cases declined rather than guessed
how_to_read: Each case is a pair of tree states and the answer a human gives. `expect: move` means exactly one moved revision per listed pair. `expect: decline` means zero moves and, where stated, one conflict row -- a declination is a correct answer here, not a miss, which is why precision and declination are scored separately.
provenance: Cases 1-6 are the behaviours 01 F5 and 02 section 10 C11 specify. Cases 7-9 are rename shapes taken from real commit history in the S1.8 soak corpus (perf/soak/corpus.json) and replayed against the fixture tree, so the corpus is not made only of the cases the implementation was written against. Every case is labelled by hand. Corpus v2: one case was mislabelled at v1 and the evaluator caught it -- see `rename-plus-an-added-function-still-moves-the-old-ones`.

cases.why: 01 F5.1 -- the same declarations at a new path. The digest matches, so the identity moved and did not disappear.
A module moved into a package is the commonest real rename and the one that most looks like a delete plus an add.

01 F5 -- a move is an exact semantic-digest match, and the digest is per REFERENT rather than per file. Every declaration in the file changes its own signature here (the class gains a base, both functions gain a parameter), so no referent is the one it was and none may move. Labelling this took two attempts: changing only a METHOD's signature left the class declaration untouched, and the class correctly moved -- which is the distinction between a file that changed and a referent that changed.

The case the corpus got wrong first, kept because getting it wrong is the point. A file that moved AND gained a declaration is not one event: the pre-existing referents moved with unchanged digests and the new one is new. `01` F5's rule is per referent, not per file, and a corpus that labelled this `no-move` would have been demanding that a correct mover orphan two identities because an unrelated function was added beside them.

02 section 10 C11 -- two candidates match one prior identity. 01 section 8 gives ambiguous-move resolution to nobody in Build 1, so the only correct answer is to decline and record the conflict for Build 3.
The same ambiguity at higher cardinality. A rule that declines at two and picks at three would be a rule nobody could state.
01 F5.3 and 00 section 5 -- absence and parse failure are indistinguishable from here, so a vanished referent is never a move and never a death. Nothing is written.
Replays the commonest rename shape in the soak corpus's own history: a module promoted into a subpackage of the same app, contents unchanged.
A whole directory renamed -- every identity beneath it moves at once. Replays a real reorganisation shape; the failure mode it guards is a mover that handles one file and orphans a package.
A rename in the same commit as an unrelated new file, which is what real commits look like. The addition must not make the move ambiguous.
